events.content:
Now I understand the API fully:

- `withTableSorting(Table)` — sorts data internally based on `column.meta.sort` (a comparator function or `true` for default comparison). Also `meta.defaultSortOrder`.
- `withTableSelection(Table)` — needs `selectedIds`, `onSelectionChange`. Selection column with checkboxes in header and rows.
- `Pagination` component for pagination.

Important: withTableSorting sorts the *data it's given*. If I paginate first and then give the table only a page of data, sorting will only sort within the page. So I should sort the full dataset myself and disable internal sorting (`disableDataSorting`), OR give the full data and let the HOC sort... no — the HOC sorts whatever data passed, then I need pagination to slice after sorting.

Options:
1. Use `withTableSorting` with `disableDataSorting`, control `sortState` myself, sort the full dataset in App, then slice the page.
2. Compose HOCs: `withTableSelection(withTableSorting(Table))`, pass full data — but then pagination slicing happens outside... that won't work because Table renders all given rows.

Actually the cleanest: control sort state in App, sort full data, slice page, pass page to table with `disableDataSorting` and controlled `sortState`/`onSortStateChange`. Sort indicators still render and handle clicks.

`withTableSelection<I, E>` infers I from SortableTable's props which include TableProps<User>. Good.

getRowDescriptor to supply row id: `getRowDescriptor={(item) => ({id: item.id})}` or use deprecated getRowId="id". getRowDescriptor is current API.

import React from 'react';
import {
  Button,
  Label,
  Pagination,
  Table,
  Text,
  withTableSelection,
  withTableSorting,
} from '@gravity-ui/uikit';
import type {TableColumnConfig, TableProps, TableSortState} from '@gravity-ui/uikit';
import {USERS, type User} from './data';

const SortableTable = withTableSorting<User>(Table as unknown as React.ComponentType<TableProps<User>>);
const DataTable = withTableSelection(SortableTable);

const collator = new Intl.Collator('en');

const columns: TableColumnConfig<User>[] = [
  {id: 'name', name: 'Name', primary: true, meta: {sort: (a, b) => collator.compare(a.name, b.name)}},
  {id: 'email', name: 'Email', meta: {sort: (a,b) => collator.compare(a.email, b.email)}},
  {id: 'role', name: 'Role', meta: {sort: ...}},

  {id: 'status', name: 'Status', template: item => <Label .../>, meta: {sort: ...}},
];
```

Wait — `meta.sort: true`? The code checks `typeof compareFunction === 'function'` else default compare. `meta.sort: true` truthy triggers enhanceColumns to make it sortable and default compare. In the .d.ts meta is `Record<string, any>` so `true` works. Default compare: `get(itemA, columnId) > get(itemB, columnId) ? 1 : -1`. For numbers fine; for strings it's case-sensitive code-unit comparison — I'll use collator comparators for strings.

const [sortState, setSortState] = React.useState<TableSortState>([{column: 'name', order: 'asc'}]);
```

Hmm, controlled sortState + disableDataSorting default: `disableDataSorting = this.isControlledState()`. When controlled (sortState prop passed), data sorting is disabled by default — exactly what I want: I sort the full dataset myself, then paginate.
